stem: A dialog's close control is a `<button>` containing only an inline SVG X icon. What is the best way to give the button an accessible name?

options.rationale: aria-label gives the button a name that assistive technology can announce even though the visible content is an icon.
alt applies to images, on an inline SVG icon it does not reliably name the button.
A title may show a tooltip, but it is not a reliable accessible name.
aria-describedby adds a description, not the name the control needs.

explanation: An icon-only button still needs a name that assistive technology can announce and voice control can target. `aria-label` on the button supplies that name. `aria-describedby` adds a description rather than a name, a `title` is not reliably exposed, and `alt` belongs to images.

references.title: W3C WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices — Providing Accessible Names and Descriptions

author: Oxypteros
